writing_rules: Write only from the evidence pack. It is the sole source of every fact, figure, level and claim.
Every client-facing claim must cite one or more allowed claim IDs in that section's claim_ids.
Copy every figure, Performance Level and product name exactly as the pack states it. Never round, convert, restate or estimate.
Never name a product the pack does not list for the option it belongs to.
Never present a claim the pack blocks, and never describe a shared result as a change or a gain.
Never recommend changing the design, and never describe the proposal as an upgrade path.
Where P20 does not support seat-to-seat bass consistency, describe bass only as output authority, physical capability and the subwoofer specification.
State a primary-seat or a secondary-seat result only where the pack states that scope's own claim, word it for that scope alone, and never present it as a result for the seating area or the room.
Sell what is strong: state a supported strength positively and stop there, and where one scope is the stronger, keep the claim to that scope rather than reporting the weaker one beside it.

The proposal is not a design review: never write that something needs attention, improvement, calibration, optimisation or further design work, and never suggest a future correction, a recalibration or an upgrade path.
Write to the client: benefit-led, dealer-safe language, with no internal parameter codes and no engineering jargon.
Keep every paragraph to one to three sentences, and keep every section inside its word limit.
Explain what each recorded result means for the room, rather than naming the number and moving on.
Return structured JSON only, in the nine sections of this contract, with no extra fields and no commentary.

sections.text: Level 1 version gives the room the format. Level 4 version gives that format the authority to feel like a serious dedicated cinema. Both retain the 9.1.6 layout, while Level 4 version is the stronger recommendation where maximum performance and headroom are the priority. The extra capability is most apparent when dialogue, score and screen effects rise together, surround and height effects fill a demanding scene, or the soundtrack calls for physical bass impact.

Both options keep the same room, screen scale, seating and 9.1.6 layout. They also share the same acoustic treatment: Artcoustic Abfuser × 8. The 15 sound positions around and above the seats remain the same, so the choice is not between different cinema formats; it is between different equipment and levels of performance within that format.

The speaker package changes at the screen, around the seating and overhead, and Level 4 version has four SUB4-12 subwoofers rather than two. Its screen stage has greater headroom for dialogue, score and effects to build together; its surround and height layers retain more presence in demanding scenes; and its bass system has greater authority for the low-frequency impact of a film soundtrack. Level 1 version has the stronger bass-extension result: both specify 16 Hz, with Level 1 version at L4 and Level 4 version at L3. That difference concerns depth, not the greater output authority Level 4 version offers for powerful bass moments.

Both options have excellent screen-channel consistency across the primary seats, and excellent bass response across the primary seats. Level 4 version's front stage reaches 116 dBC (L4), compared with 106 dBC (L3) for Level 1 version; its non-screen result is 108 dBC (OH) (L4), compared with 100 dBC (FW) (L2). For low-frequency output, Level 4 version reaches 118 dBC (L4), compared with 115 dBC (L3). In a film, those differences matter as the score and effects swell, movement fills the room, and bass-heavy moments demand physical scale.

Both options provide 15 discrete channels, placing sound positions around and above the seats. Across the primary seats, Level 4 version has excellent screen consistency; its overhead spacing is great, and overhead level consistency is great, helping the height layer remain balanced across the main listening positions. Level 1 version has good speaker spacing across the primary seats, supporting clear movement between the screen and side channels. Its front wide positions bridge the screen and side speakers more effectively than Level 4 version's, a difference that helps connect screen action with effects moving out to the sides.

Level 4 version provides more room for the screen speakers to carry dialogue, music and effects as a scene builds; its result is 116 dBC (L4), against 106 dBC (L3) for Level 1 version. Around and above the audience, the difference is also substantial: 108 dBC (OH) (L4) for Level 4 version versus 100 dBC (FW) (L2) for Level 1 version. In a dense action sequence, that additional capability helps surround and height effects keep their presence alongside the main soundtrack. Level 4 version's 118 dBC (L4) bass result, compared with 115 dBC (L3), brings greater authority and physical impact to low-frequency effects.

Both options have tonal consistency across the screen channels, so voices and effects stay consistent from left to right. Across the primary seats, screen timbre is excellent, as is surround and overhead timbre; this supports natural-sounding effects as they move around and above the audience. Bass extension reaches 16 Hz in both designs; Level 1 version is L4 and Level 4 version is L3 for this measure of how far down the system reaches. Bass response is excellent across the primary seats in both options.

Level 1 version remains a credible 9.1.6 design, retaining the same room, screen, seating and sound positions as Level 4 version. The difference is the equipment and the performance reserve: Level 4 version is the stronger recommendation when maximum performance and headroom are the priority. Its greater capacity across the screen, surround and height layers, together with the additional bass output authority, is heard when a soundtrack grows dense and its largest effects arrive.

This comparison is based on the saved visual and technical report evidence for the Level 4 version and the Level 1 version. The option names and the performance statements in this proposal follow those reports; figures and product details are included only where the comparison evidence states them.
